name: Red pink
lede: Red pink is a vivid, slightly bluish pink-red, a name that comes from a color survey rather than from any tradition.

sections.title: A survey name
sections.body:
The name appears in the xkcd color survey and in no other source in our library [1]. The books do not discuss it, so its coiner is undocumented. Our data pairs it with a near-duplicate, "reddish pink", about 1.1 units away, and with [[pink-red]] as its closest named neighbor; its closest match among the established names is [[cerise]], 7.7 units off [1].

It sits at the border between two words with a long history. In Pliny's day, Pastoureau notes, Romans already told some fifteen reds apart in porphyry and purple cloth, while naming only two or three greens [2]. Pink, later, became one of the shades on the margins of red, and from the later Middle Ages fashion favored darker reds and shades bordering on red, such as pink and purple [3].

sections.title: Why pink is a red
sections.body: Eckstut and Eckstut explain pink in light terms: most of the light reaching the eye is red, and the rest is white [4]. Red pink is the saturated end of that, close to [[red]] and far from [[pink]] in the pale sense.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This is a screen color at #FA2A55 with a lightness of about 55 and a chroma of 81 [1]. We did not compute a painting count for it; the color is more saturated than almost any varnished museum paint, so a close match is rare.
